name: simulate-roth-conversion-boundary
why: Measured reach for the pure aggregate Roth-conversion planner and the caller band that invokes it, publishes its snapshot and replays its temporary RMD reservation. Block T's four hostile members run in all four equivalence modes: T1 combines deferred-RMD Map owner order, a reverse Plan-order multi-account reserve, duplicate Roth ids with distinct opening balances, two-owner exact-cent allocation and ordered source/destination publication; T2 makes the required subtract/add restoration move a binary64 leaf and exercises counterfactual rollback/re-entry; T3 reaches household refusal; T4 reaches an allocated result with no convertible owner, slices or draws. Helper identity and the reservation stream's cross-owner operation order are guarded separately by the focused helper/delegation suites: a JSON dump can observe neither object identity nor the order of subtract/add operations on disjoint owner states when their final economic values agree.

entries.label: private Plan-order planning shadows and reservation stream
owner-order and reverse Plan-order deferred-RMD reservation
entries.note: T1 reaches both owners, skips nontraditional and other-owner rows, exhausts p1's one-dollar tail, skips its zero-dollar IRA and continues into the earlier source. T2 supplies the cancellation-sensitive reservation. Inherited-account exclusion is pinned by the focused helper suite. The remaining cold nullish owner fallback is a supported structural contract but cannot be selected by corpus data because Plan validation requires every traditional account to name an individual owner.

readingTheCounts: A member count proves that at least one line in the named range executed. The reach command additionally fails on any cold executable whole line inside a reached range. JavaScript line coverage cannot distinguish every operand or branch sharing a physical line, so the report's cold sub-line regions and these notes must be read together with the focused helper and hostile delegation tests.
